extracted.intended_audience: authors, researchers, institutional press officers and journalists interacting with Nature Portfolio journals (esp. Nature Human Behaviour)
extracted.subtask_short: press and embargo policy for authors
extracted.subtask_description: Policies governing when and how authors, institutions and journalists may publicize material submitted to or accepted by Nature Portfolio journals, including rules on embargoes, press releases, preprints and communication with the media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct solicitation of media by authors
rubrics_metrics.description: We strongly discourage authors and potential authors from direct solicitation of media coverage of material they have submitted to Nature and the Nature Portfolio journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should not directly solicit media coverage of work under submission. This applies both to submissions and to interim stages — authors are strongly discouraged from seeking media attention before publication. See related guidance on preprints and conference presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of permitted media discussion (embargo window)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted contributions can be discussed with the media only once the publication date has been confirmed and no more than a week before the publication date under our embargo conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may discuss accepted papers with media only in the specified embargo window (generally within one week before publication) and only when the publication date is confirmed. Any discussion outside this window risks breaching the journal's embargo policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release distribution and embargoed access for journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature produces and distributes press releases summarizing upcoming content to a list of registered journalists. Journalists receive access to the full text of papers about a week before publication on a password-protected website, together with other relevant material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists are encouraged to read the full version of any papers they wish to cover and are given the names and contact details of corresponding authors. The content of the press release and the papers is embargoed until the time and date clearly stated on the press release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial highlighting of especially newsworthy papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers that are deemed especially newsworthy are highlighted by a brief summary on the press release for that journal, written by the editors and the press office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a paper is highlighted, authors may receive calls or emails from the media during the embargo window; authors are encouraged to cooperate so that media coverage is accurate and balanced. The highlight is editorially determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors' own publicity must adhere to embargo and be coordinated
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors whose papers are scheduled for publication may also arrange their own publicity (for instance through their institutional press offices), but they must strictly adhere to our media embargo and are advised to coordinate their own publicity with our press office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional or personal publicity activities are permitted only if they strictly follow the embargo conditions and the journal's timing; coordination with the journal's press office is recommended to avoid premature release or conflicting messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and justification for embargo policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nature Portfolio journals believe that their media embargo serves scientists, authors, journalists and the public by releasing information in a way that provides fair and equal access to the media, allowing it to provide informed comment based on the complete and final version of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embargoes enable journalists to obtain informed reactions from independent researchers and rely on peer review; premature release denies journalists that confidence and can remove the opportunity for informed comment. Authors and institutions should respect embargoes for these reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for embargo breaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists who break our embargoes have been removed from the press-release circulation list, and we shall continue to use this sanction when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal enforces embargo rules by removing offending journalists from press-distribution lists and may apply other sanctions as appropriate to maintain fair access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprints and conference presentations do not constitute prior publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Portfolio journals do not wish to hinder communication among researchers. Neither conference presentations nor posting on recognized preprint servers constitute prior publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers are supported in sharing drafts on established preprint servers and speaking at meetings; such exposure does not preclude submission to Nature journals. See the journal's linked policies for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on media communication about preprints and conference material
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers may respond to requests from the media in response to a preprint or conference presentation by providing explanation or clarification of the work or information about its context; media coverage will not hinder editorial handling but may reduce or pre-empt coverage at the time of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When speaking about preprints, researchers should make clear that the paper has not yet undergone peer review, that the findings are provisional and that conclusions may change. The journal also recommends reporters indicate that preprints have not been peer reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of the peer review and editorial process
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are expected to keep the details of the peer review and editorial process confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While discussing work (including preprints), authors must not disclose confidential details of peer review or editorial handling. For further clarification on any communication, contact the Nature Portfolio press office by e-mail.
